output.summary: Four plays in 90 days. Rescue trials that never send data. Spend $400/month on German and French cookie-banner search ads. Pitch EU agencies that sell GDPR-ready sites. Run one capped AI-traffic launch post. The trial rescue is the biggest, most bankable lever; the other three test new demand cheaply.
output.positioning: The simple, cookieless alternative to Google Analytics. No personal data and no cookie banner for your stats. A script 54x smaller than GA. Independent, profitable and EU-based, trusted by 21,000+ paying subscribers.

audiences.name: Stalled trial users
audiences.hypothesis: Many trials never connect a site, so they never see value or pay.
audiences.evidence: Assumption to verify with trial data. The no-card 30-day trial lowers the bar to sign up but not to install.

audiences.name: DACH and French site owners with cookie-banner pain
audiences.hypothesis: Local-language consent searches cost less and convert better than crowded English 'GA alternative' terms.
audiences.evidence: No cookies or personal data, plus an EU base, matches DSGVO/RGPD-driven searches. Click costs are unverified until Keyword Planner is checked.

audiences.name: EU web agencies selling GDPR-friendly builds
audiences.hypothesis: Agencies that already market privacy will add cookieless analytics to every client site.
audiences.evidence: The site names agencies and white-label as audiences, and the Growth and Business plans allow multiple sites. Low confidence: no partner incentive is confirmed.

audiences.name: Indie hackers, SaaS founders and publishers curious about AI traffic
audiences.hypothesis: An honest post on AI-tool referrers, using Plausible's own public data, can reach HN and Reddit front pages.
audiences.evidence: The site says Plausible shows visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude. This needs checking before publishing.

deliverables: 4 behavior-triggered emails (day 2 platform setup guide, day 5 GA import, day 10 personal help reply, day 25 trial-ending reminder)
Dashboard banner copy for sites with no data
50/50 holdout split logic spec
Tracking sheet: first-data rate within 7 days, trial-to-paid by arm
dependencies: Engineering hook to flag 'no pageview at 48h' and to randomize
Support person to answer day-10 replies
Baseline trial counts from last month
channels.measurement: Holdout vs. treatment first-data rate within 7 days and trial-to-paid rate, after 200 trials per arm.

channels.name: German and French cookie-banner search ads

deliverables: German and French exact/phrase keyword lists with brand and job/free negatives
Responsive search ads in both languages using only confirmed claims
UTM-tagged links to the migration and vs-GA pages
Weekly cost-per-trial report

'Free Trial Started' goal imported as the Google Ads conversion
Decision on whether landing pages need German/French versions

channels.name: EU agency personal outreach
channels.why: One agency account can bring many client sites. Costs owner time, not ad budget.
deliverables: Qualified list of 200 EU agencies that market GDPR/DSGVO builds
Two email angles (client-banner pain vs. all client sites in one account) plus 2 follow-ups
Simple pipeline sheet: sent, replied, trial, paid
dependencies: Owner approval of the email copy
Sending inbox and LinkedIn account
Confirm that agency and white-label page claims are current

channels.why: Low cost, high upside, and it fits a transparent brand voice. Most posts won't hit the front page.

5-minute 'check your AI traffic' how-to
Show HN title and 2-3 subreddit versions
UTM links and a 14-day results note

Owner confirms the exact AI-referral claims
Subreddit rules allow the post

experiments.name: Trial rescue holdout
experiments.hypothesis: Nudging trials with no pageviews at 48h raises the first-data rate by 5+ points and lifts trial-to-paid.
experiments.population: New trials with zero pageviews 48h after signup, randomized 50/50
experiments.primaryMetric: First pageview received within 7 days of signup
guardrails: Support reply load handled within 1 business day
Trial-to-paid rate not lower in the treatment arm
experiments.stoppingRule: Stop at 200 trials per arm or 4 weeks. Kill if the lift is under 3 points. Roll out if it's 5+ points and trial-to-paid improves.

experiments.name: DE vs FR consent-pain search ads
experiments.hypothesis: At least one language delivers trials under $40 each.
experiments.population: Searchers in DE/AT/CH and FR using consent and cookie-free analytics terms
guardrails: Trials connect a site at or above the site-wide rate
experiments.stoppingRule: Judge at $600 total spend. Kill if cost per trial is over $80 or there are under 5 trials. Move the full budget to a language under $40.

experiments.name: Agency outreach subject angle
experiments.hypothesis: The client-banner-pain angle gets more replies than the multi-site convenience angle.
experiments.population: First 100 qualified EU agencies, alternating between the two angles
guardrails: Personal, one-to-one emails only, with an easy opt-out
experiments.stoppingRule: After 100 messages, kill if there are under 3 replies or zero trials. Scale to 400 agencies if 5%+ reply and 2+ agencies trial a client site.

experiments.name: AI-traffic launch post
experiments.hypothesis: An honest AI-referrer post brings 1,000+ visits and 10+ trials.
experiments.population: HN and Reddit readers reached by a single post
guardrails: Only Plausible's own site data, never customer data
experiments.stoppingRule: Kill if under 1,000 visits in 48h or under 10 trials in 14 days, and move the hours to agencies. Over 50 trials: localize the post for the DE/FR ad pages.

Small team, so owner time is capped at about 4 hours a week, plus 6 hours once for the launch post (assumption)
No legal compliance promises: describe what the product does, not GDPR outcomes
Only confirmed claims in copy: 54x smaller script, no cookies or personal data, 21,000+ paying subscribers, 313B+ pageviews, independent, self-funded, profitable, EU-based
Customer names and quotes stay out until the owner confirms them
output.measurementPlan: Use Plausible itself: a 'Free Trial Started' goal with UTMs per play (gads_de, gads_fr, outreach_agency, hn, reddit), plus billing data for trial-to-paid. One weekly sheet tracks trials, first-data rate, cost per trial and new paid by source. The trial rescue uses a true holdout. The other plays are judged against their kill and scale thresholds.

plays.name: Rescue trials that never connect a site
plays.oneLiner: Automatically nudge trial users whose dashboard has no pageviews 48 hours after signup, and offer them setup help.
plays.audience: New 30-day trial users whose site has sent zero pageviews by hour 48.
plays.trigger: No pageview received 48 hours after signup, checked again on day 5 and day 10.
plays.hook: Your dashboard is still empty. Most setups take one snippet. Here is the exact step for your site builder, or reply and we'll check it with you.
plays.mechanic: Emails sent when the user does (or doesn't do) something, plus a banner in the dashboard. Day 2: setup guide matched to their platform. Day 5: offer the GA import. Day 10: a person replies to help. Day 25: a plain reminder that the trial is ending. Send half the eligible trials the sequence and hold back the other half to measure the lift.
plays.assetUsed: The current 30-day no-card trial, the Google Analytics import, the live demo, and the small, light script (54x smaller than GA), which makes setup quick.
plays.biggestUnknown: What share of trials never connect a site today. If it's already small, this play has little room to help.
plays.test: Randomly split trial signups that hit the no-data trigger 50/50 for 4 weeks, or until each side has 200 trials. Compare first-data rate within 7 days and trial-to-paid rate.
plays.killIf: After 200 trials per side, the share of rescued users who connect their site is less than 3 percentage points above the hold-out group.
plays.scaleIf: First-data rate rises by 5 or more points and trial-to-paid improves. Then roll it out to every trial and add the same trigger for 'connected but no goals set'.
plays.firstActionToday: Pull last month's trials and count how many had zero pageviews at 48 hours and at day 30. That number sizes this play.
plays.climbosCanDo: Write the 4-email rescue sequence and the dashboard banner copy, set up the split-test plan, and build the tracking sheet.

plays.name: Cookie-banner pain search ads in German and French
plays.oneLiner: Spend $400/month on Google Search ads in German and French, aimed at people trying to remove cookie banners or replace GA, instead of the crowded English 'GA alternative' terms.
plays.audience: Site owners in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and France searching in their own language for analytics without cookies or consent banners.
plays.trigger: Searches like 'Webanalyse ohne Cookies', 'Google Analytics Alternative DSGVO', 'Cookie-Banner entfernen Analytics', 'analytics sans cookies' and 'alternative Google Analytics RGPD'.
plays.hook: Ad copy: 'Webanalyse ohne Cookies. Keine personenbezogenen Daten, kein Cookie-Banner für Ihre Statistik. Unabhängig, aus der EU. 30 Tage kostenlos testen.' (English: 'Analytics without cookies. No personal data, no cookie banner for your stats. Independent, from the EU. Try it free for 30 days.')
plays.mechanic: Exact-match and phrase-match keywords only, with brand terms excluded. Send clicks to the existing migration and 'vs Google Analytics' pages. Count a Free Trial Started as the conversion. In 3 months, $1,200 at a $3-6 click (assumed, set against the WordStream $5.26 average) gives about 200-400 clicks. At 5.1% trial rate (Unbounce) that's about 10-20 trials, which at 9-18% trial-to-paid means about 1-4 customers. Upside comes if local-language clicks are cheaper.
plays.assetUsed: No cookies or personal data, so no banners or consent forms. Independent, self-funded, EU-based company. 21,000+ paying subscribers. The 30-day no-card trial.
plays.biggestUnknown: Real click prices for German and French consent-related searches, and whether the landing pages need translating for these visitors to convert.
plays.test: Run two ad groups: German consent-pain terms and French consent-pain terms. $400/month split evenly, judged after 4 weeks or $600 spent.
plays.killIf: Cost per trial is above $80, or fewer than 5 trials come in, after $600 spent.
plays.scaleIf: Cost per trial is under $40 and trials connect a site at or above the site-wide rate. Then shift the whole budget to the winning language and add Dutch and Nordic terms.
plays.firstActionToday: Run the German and French keyword lists through Google Keyword Planner and check search volume and top-of-page bid ranges before spending anything.
plays.climbosCanDo: Build the keyword lists, negative keywords, and responsive search ads in German and French using only confirmed claims, and send a weekly cost-per-trial report.

plays.name: EU agencies that sell 'GDPR-ready' websites
plays.oneLiner: Send short personal emails to 200 web agencies that already promise clients GDPR-friendly sites, suggesting Plausible as the analytics they add to every build.
plays.audience: Small EU web and WordPress agencies whose own sites market GDPR, DSGVO or privacy-friendly builds.
plays.trigger: The agency's service page mentions GDPR/DSGVO compliance, or its portfolio sites show a consent banner loaded mainly for analytics.
plays.hook: You already sell privacy-friendly sites. Analytics without cookies means one less thing behind the banner on every client build, and you see all client sites in one account.
plays.mechanic: Personal cold email and LinkedIn messages, 40 per week for 5 weeks, each with one line specific to that agency. The ask is to start a trial on one client site. Assumptions: 3-8% reply, about 40% of replies start a trial, 25% of those pay. Each agency account can cover several sites.
plays.assetUsed: Multi-site and team access on the Growth and Business plans (from the site), the white-label/agency pages, no cookies or personal data, and EU base.
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether agencies switch analytics for clients without a referral or partner incentive, and none is confirmed.
plays.test: Send 100 messages in 2.5 weeks using two subject angles (client-banner pain vs. managing many sites in one place). Track reply rate and trial starts.
plays.killIf: Fewer than 3 replies, or zero trials, from the first 100 messages.
plays.scaleIf: 5% or more reply and at least 2 agencies trial a client site. Then extend to 400 agencies and turn the winning angle into a dedicated agency page.
plays.firstActionToday: Build a list of 50 EU agencies whose service pages mention GDPR or DSGVO, and note the analytics script on each agency's own portfolio sites.
plays.climbosCanDo: Research and qualify the agency list, write the two personal email versions and follow-ups for owner approval, and track replies in a simple pipeline.

plays.name: 'How much of your traffic comes from AI?' launch post
plays.oneLiner: A transparent founder post showing how Plausible's own public dashboard reports visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude, launched once on Hacker News and Reddit.
plays.audience: Indie hackers, SaaS founders, developers and publishers who are curious whether AI tools send them traffic.
plays.trigger: The current interest in AI search sending visitors. Launch on a weekday morning, US Eastern time.
plays.hook: We looked at where AI chat tools show up in our own referrers. Here is what a cookieless dashboard shows, and how to check yours in 5 minutes.
plays.mechanic: One honest post using only Plausible's own site data from its public live demo. No customer data, which keeps the 'we don't sell or use your data' promise. Submit to Show HN plus relevant subreddits that allow it. Capped at 6 owner hours and $100 to boost on Reddit only if it gets traction without paid help. Assumption: a front-page HN post brings 10k-30k visits. At 1-2% trial and about 15% paid, that's 15-90 customers. Most posts don't reach the front page, so p50 is low.
plays.assetUsed: The public live demo, the AI-referral reporting the site describes (check exact claims first), the 54x lighter script, and the independent, profitable, self-funded story.
funnel: Visit to post and live demo
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether Plausible's own referrer data shows a story interesting enough to reach the front page.
plays.test: Publish once, then measure trials with UTM tags from HN and Reddit for 14 days.
plays.killIf: Under 1,000 visits in 48 hours, or under 10 trials in 14 days. Don't repost; move the hours back to the agency play.
plays.scaleIf: Over 50 trials from the post. Then turn it into a German and French version for the search-ad landing pages, and a quarterly update post.
plays.firstActionToday: Open Plausible's own dashboard, filter referrers for ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude, and decide whether there's a real, shareable finding.
plays.climbosCanDo: Draft the post and the 5-minute how-to from the owner's real dashboard numbers, write a short HN title and Reddit versions, and set up UTM links.

output.portfolioNote: I'd put the $500/month into German- and French-language search ads ($400) plus one capped launch test ($100). Fixing the existing trials is likely the biggest lever, because 21,000+ paying subscribers suggests strong trial volume. [NEEDS FACT: How many trials start each month, and what share become paid?] Benchmarks used: no-card trials convert 8.9% to paid (ChartMogul 2026) up to 18.2% (First Page Sage). SaaS landing pages convert 3.8%, or 5.1% from Google search (Unbounce). The average Google Ads click costs $5.26 (WordStream/LocaliQ 2025). Scores are impact, confidence, ease and speed, each out of 10.

output.summary: Four plays over 60 days, $300/month on Meta (about $600 total), about 3 owner hours a week. The base is an order-by countdown to people who already know Tartine. Office outreach targets group orders. Meta ads reach Tartine Bread readers outside California with Goldbelly shipping. A capped gift-guide pitch is the long shot.
output.positioning: Your holiday table, baked by Tartine: a San Francisco bakery since 2002 that you can pre-order for pickup or get shipped nationwide through Goldbelly. Lead with craft and planning ahead. Make no 'best' or price claims.

audiences.name: Bay Area regulars and recent site visitors
audiences.hypothesis: They already want Tartine for the holidays. They need a clear order-by date and a direct link to act before the deadline.
audiences.evidence: The site already runs a holiday pastry and pies pre-order banner. Insights list 4 Bay Area locations with a regular local customer base.

audiences.name: SF office managers and executive assistants
audiences.hypothesis: They plan December team events 1-3 weeks ahead. A timely, personal note with an order-by date will win some group orders.
audiences.evidence: Special order cakes need seven days' notice and are picked up at 600 Guerrero St. Digital Bloom reports timeline hooks get about 2.3x the replies.

audiences.name: Tartine Bread readers outside California
audiences.hypothesis: Home bakers who know the book but can't visit will buy a shipped holiday order for themselves or as a gift.
audiences.evidence: Tartine ships nationwide through Goldbelly. The site links to the Tartine books.

audiences.name: Gift-guide readers
audiences.hypothesis: A link in an online holiday guide sends ready-to-buy gift shoppers to Goldbelly or gift cards.
audiences.evidence: The Infatuation's SF holiday pie guide already lists Tartine, per play research. The site sells gift cards online.

channels.name: Owned countdown: email, Google Business Profile Offer posts, counter QR cards
channels.why: Cheapest reach to people who already buy. Email alone is the largest part of the forecast.
deliverables: 3 emails: announce, halfway, last call
Weekly Offer post on each Bay Area Google Business Profile
Counter and bag QR card text
Unique UTM link or QR code per touchpoint
dependencies: Confirmed holiday order-by date and pickup details
Access to the email platform and Google Business Profiles
Counter space and printing
channels.measurement: Attributed pre-orders per send, post and QR code via UTMs and the 'How did you hear about us?' field. Target at least 0.26% placed orders per send (Branvas benchmark).

channels.name: Meta ads: local retargeting plus Tartine Bread readers outside CA
channels.why: Two $150/month ad sets. One converts warm locals. The other is the only scalable way to reach out-of-state book readers for Goldbelly.
deliverables: Retargeting ad set: site visitors from the last 30 days, Instagram engagers, small radius around SF locations
Interest ad set: sourdough and baking-book interests, California excluded, 2 creatives (bread and holiday pastry)
UTM links to the pre-order page and the Goldbelly shop
Weekly spend, CPC, CTR and orders report
dependencies: Meta Business Manager and pixel access
3 product photos Tartine has rights to use
Goldbelly dashboard showing orders by date
channels.measurement: CPC against the $0.72 benchmark and cost per attributed order against the $38.57 CPA benchmark (2025 WordStream, as compiled by Fibbler/Enrich Labs). Goldbelly orders are compared with the prior 4 weeks.

channels.name: Office holiday group orders
channels.why: A few group orders can outweigh many single pre-orders. December party planning matches the outreach timing.
deliverables: List of 150 office managers and EAs near SF locations
Personal email and LinkedIn message plus 1 follow-up
Shared sheet tracking replies, orders and order size
dependencies: [NEEDS FACT: Does Tartine take catering or large group orders, and through which page or contact?]
One named person to answer group-order replies
channels.measurement: Replies per 100 messages (benchmark 0.45% to 3-5%, per Belkins and Digital Bloom), group orders and order size.

channels.name: Gift-guide pitch blitz (capped)
channels.why: Low-cost long shot. One placement can send gift buyers to Goldbelly and gift cards.
deliverables: 25 personal pitches to online holiday gift and pre-order guide editors
1 follow-up each
Log of replies and placements
dependencies: Approved pitch angle
Named press contact
channels.measurement: Guide placements with a link, plus UTM clicks to Goldbelly and gift cards. Hard cap of 6 hours.

experiments.name: Countdown email holdout
experiments.hypothesis: The 3-email countdown drives pre-orders that would not have happened anyway.
experiments.population: Email subscribers. A random 10% is held out from all countdown emails.
experiments.primaryMetric: Holiday pre-orders per 1,000 subscribers, mailed group vs holdout (matched by email at checkout)
experiments.stoppingRule: Ends at the holiday order deadline. Drop the holdout early only if the email platform cannot split the list.

experiments.name: Shipping ad creative: bread vs holiday pastry
experiments.hypothesis: Book readers respond more to a bread-led ad than to a holiday pastry ad.
experiments.population: US Meta users with sourdough and baking-book interests, California excluded
experiments.primaryMetric: Goldbelly link clicks per $ and attributed Goldbelly orders
experiments.stoppingRule: Move the budget to the winner after each version gets 5,000 impressions. Stop both if 0 extra Goldbelly orders after $150.

experiments.name: Countdown vs same weeks last year
experiments.hypothesis: The full owned and paid countdown lifts total holiday pre-orders above last year's same weeks.
experiments.population: All holiday pre-orders at Bay Area pickup
experiments.primaryMetric: Weekly holiday pre-orders vs the same week last year
guardrails: No rise in missed or late pickups
experiments.stoppingRule: Ends at the order deadline. Pause Meta retargeting if CPC is over $1.50 after $75 or 0 attributed orders after $150.

experiments.name: Office outreach opener: pies vs special order cake
experiments.hypothesis: Leading with pre-ordered holiday pies gets more replies than leading with a special order cake, because pies need less planning.
experiments.population: 150 SF office managers and EAs, split evenly
guardrails: Every message is personal, with no bulk blasts
experiments.stoppingRule: Stop if fewer than 2 replies from the first 100 messages, or 0 orders after 150.

constraints: Ad budget is $300/month on Meta, paid directly to the platform. That is about $600 over 60 days.
About 3 owner hours a week. ClimbOS drafts everything and the owner approves.
Special order cakes need seven days' notice, with pickup only at 600 Guerrero St.
Shipping runs through Goldbelly, so attribution depends on its reporting.
No prices, reviews or testimonials are confirmed, so copy cannot use them.
No 'best' claims, fake deadlines or fake scarcity. Only the real order-by date is used.
output.measurementPlan: One sheet, updated weekly. Every touchpoint gets a unique UTM link or QR code. The pre-order form adds a 'How did you hear about us?' field. Goldbelly orders are compared with the prior 4 weeks. Total pre-orders are compared with the same weeks last year. The email holdout gives the cleanest read on email's incremental lift.

firstActions.why: Every email, post, ad and pitch hangs on this date.

firstActions.why: The office play can't launch without it.

firstActions.why: Without these there is no attribution and no baseline.

firstActions.why: Owned channels and retargeting are the fastest orders.

firstActions.title: Build the 150-contact office list and the 25-editor pitch list
firstActions.why: Outreach has to land before December planning closes.

output.diagnosis: Demand for holiday pre-orders already exists, but the message is one banner on a crowded home page, with no countdown and no source tracking. The fastest gain is pushing a clear order-by date through channels Tartine already owns, then measuring what works.
output.affordableCac: Average order value and margin are not confirmed, so true affordable CAC is unknown. Working ceilings (assumption): $20 per local pre-order and $38 per Goldbelly order, matching the $38.57 Food & Beverage CPA benchmark (WordStream 2025, via Fibbler). Revise these once order values are known.

notDoing.why: $300/month is too thin to split. Branded searches likely already find Tartine without paying (assumption).
It won't rank inside a 60-day holiday window.

notDoing.channel: New organic social programs (TikTok, daily posting)
notDoing.why: Too much owner time. Instagram is used only as a source for the ad audience.
Too little information on that audience, and the goal is US holiday pre-orders and catering.
No budget, and the results are hard to attribute in 60 days.

northStar.baseline: 0 attributed today, because nothing is tagged. Last year's same-week pre-order totals, pulled by the owner, serve as the total-volume baseline.
northStar.target: About 90 attributed orders in 60 days: p50 sum of the plays (80 countdown, 8 shipping, 4 office). Range about 28-232. Assumption-based, and moves with the real email list size.

leadingIndicators.weeklyTarget: CPC at or below $0.72 (benchmark). CTR at least 0.8%.

plays.killIf: Fewer than 2 replies from the first 50 result cards, or the 40-hour cap is reached before launch.
plays.scaleIf: 5 or more replies and at least 1 qualified call from the first 50 cards. Then finish all 30 categories and plan to refresh the index every quarter.
plays.firstActionToday: Choose the first 5 SaaS categories and write 10 buyer-intent prompts for each, reusing the snapshot prompts.
plays.climbosCanDo: Run and log the prompts, tally citation counts for each category, draft the report and the result-card emails, and draft the pitches to podcasts and newsletters for your approval.

output.portfolioNote: Four plays at $0 ad spend. Combined median estimate: about 20 qualified discovery calls in 90 days. That figure is an assumption built from the base rates cited in each play, not a promise. The bankable play is cold outreach that opens with a free AI-answer gap snapshot, which shows prospects your AEO work before any call. The two creative plays use warm channels most agencies ignore: past-client marketers who have moved to new companies, and VC firms' portfolio companies. The moonshot reuses the snapshot data in a public study and is capped at 40 hours. Owner time is about 6-8 hours a week, and ClimbOS does the drafting and research. Track every play the same way: a UTM link on each Calendly link, the form's 'how did you hear about Animalz' answer, and a weekly count of calls that fit your ideal client (B2B SaaS, a real content budget, a decision-maker on the call). Scores are impact, confidence and ease, each out of 10.
